claims.text: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys with dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The initial material may be an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Conventionally processed eutectic high-entropy alloys retain dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The intervention consists of tailored thermo-mechanical processing.
Rolling and annealing are suitable examples of the proposed tailored thermo-mechanical processing.
The relevant structural mediator is a dual-phase lamellar microstructure containing FCC and BCC phases.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing refines the grain size while retaining the duplex lamellar character.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing reduces interlamellar spacing.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing introduces defects that act as nucleation sites for deformation twinning.
Deformation twinning generated through the proposed defect-nucleation mechanism improves both strength and ductility.
The processed material will have higher yield strength than the conventional or as-cast baseline.
The processed material will have higher room-temperature tensile ductility than the conventional or as-cast baseline.
The intervention may produce ultrahigh strength together with excellent ductility.
The hypothesis is limited to eutectic high-entropy alloys with dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The result depends on the particular processing route, processing conditions, alloy composition, and prior processing history.
A controlled room-temperature tensile comparison between tailored thermo-mechanically processed and conventionally processed lamellar-colony material can test the hypothesis.
Failure to improve both yield strength and tensile ductility relative to the conventional baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
